newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: China angry at Cambodia-Taiwan aviation pact.
newsitem.headline: China angry at Cambodia-Taiwan aviation pact.

text.p: China has expressed anger at reports of a secret aviation pact signed between Cambodia and Taiwan.

"The Chinese side is firmly opposed...that those countries having diplomatic relations with China establish official air links with Taiwan," said a Chinese Embassy statement, received by Reuters on Wednesday.
"In case those countries intend to establish non-governmental air links with Taiwan, they must get the permission from the Chinese government beforehand," it added.
The statement did not say if Beijing planned any punitive action.
A Civil Aeronautics Administration spokeswoman told Reuters in Taipei on January 27 that Taiwan and Cambodia had signed an agreement allowing both countries to operate commercial flights.
EVA Airways was expected to be the Taiwan carrier.

Taiwan's United Evening News said at the time the deal had been signed in secret to avoid pressure from China, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province ineligible for international diplomatic ties since a civil war split them in 1949.

Cambodia's co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen have stressed their commitment to a one-China policy while saying they welcome investment and businessmen from Taiwan, which maintains a trade office in Phnom Penh.
Beijing was one of the architects of the 1991 Cambodian peace accord and recognised the coalition government that emerged in U.N.-sponsored 1993 elections.
